subject: arg_refactor seg faulting + doc argument format

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: arg_refactor seg faulting + doc argument format
parts:
To investigate print on arg_refactor, I tried running
a model and got a seg fault without any error.

Here's the model and data:

temp2/arr.stan
|
data {
int<lower=1> N[2];
int<lower=0> y_1[N[1]];
int<lower=0> y_2[N[2]];
}
transformed data {
int b[3];
b <- rep_array(10,3);
}
parameters {
real y;
}
model {
y ~ normal(0,1);
print("HELLO",b[1],"BYE",b);
}
|

temp2/arr.data.R
|
N <- c(2, 3)
y_1 <- c(15,25)
y_2 <- c(10,100,1000);
|

And here's the shell behavior:

|
/temp2$ ./arr sample data=arr.data.R
Segmentation fault: 11
|

Even if I'm calling it wrong, it shouldn't seg fault.

From the help for sample, I don't see the data arg. This is what
I meant by unfolding the arguments so that as we drill down, we get
a complete picture relative to where we're at.

|
~/temp2$ ./arr sample help
sample
Bayesian inference with Markov Chain Monte Carlo
Valid subarguments: num_samples, num_warmup, save_warmup, thin, adapt, algorithm
|

Data is mentioned at the top level:

|
~/temp2$ ./arr help
Usage: ./arr <arg1> <subarg1_1> ... <subarg1_m> ... <arg_n> <subarg_n_1> ... <subarg_n_m>

Begin by selecting amongst the following inference methods and diagnostics,
sample Bayesian inference with Markov Chain Monte Carlo
optimize Point estimation
diagnose Model diagnostics

Or see help information with
help Prints help
help-all Prints entire argument tree

Additional configuration available by specifying
id Unique process identifier
data Input data file
init Initialization method: "x" initializes randomly bewteen [-x, x], "0" initializes to 0, anything else
identifies a file of values
random Random number configuration
output File output options

See ./arr <arg1> [ help | help-all ] for details on individual arguments.
|

It mentions "data", but doesn't specify whether it's an arg or subarg, which
seem to be the only kinds of arguments, and nothing tells me that I need
data=foo. The specific help for data is better, and it's great it works
without a subcommand:

|
~/temp2$ ./arr data help
data=<string>
Input data file
Valid values: All
Defaults to ""
|

Can you change valid values line from "All" to something like "path to
data file"?

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] arg_refactor seg faulting + doc argument format
parts: > Even if I'm calling it wrong, it shouldn't seg fault.
Bad push a few hours ago on my part. Fixed and pushed.
> From the help for sample, I don't see the data arg.

Data does not derive from sample -- it exists for all methods (for example, we need it whether we're sampling, optimizing, or diagnosing). It's one of the top-level arguments, which is why it only shows up when you call ./model help or ./model help-all

> Can you change valid values line from "All" to something like "path to
> data file"?
